title: QuantEvolve: Automating Quantitative Strategy Discovery through Multi-Agent Evolutionary Framework

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary discovery of quantitative trading strategies
mechanism.populationDetail: Multiple island-local strategy populations evolve with a shared QD feature map and periodic top-10% migration to neighboring islands.
mechanism.archiveDetail: A MAP-Elites-style multidimensional feature map preserves the best-performing strategy per behavioral cell; a separate archive also retains rejected candidates.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The QD feature map and rejected-candidate archive form a shared evolutionary database alongside island-local populations; the paper does not fully specify island-pool survivor replacement.
mechanism.generationDetail: Initialization generates seed strategies from category/schema descriptions; evolutionary steps form hypotheses from one parent and contextual cousins, then the Coding Team broadly revises the current program or may try a new approach.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Backtest metrics and strategy analyses feed the Evaluation Team; its extracted insights are included in future Research Agent prompts and curated every 50 generations.
mechanism.parentSelection: fixed_probability_mixture: alpha-weighted uniform sampling from local QD elites and (1-alpha)-weighted uniform sampling from the selected island population; alpha=0.5.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The island is selected randomly first; best-parent and diverse-parent are two branches of the same fixed alpha mixture. Cousins are contextual references, not additional true parents.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A periodically curated, island-specific insight repository provides accumulated natural-language institutional memory across generations; current taxonomy captures feedback reuse but not this persistent knowledge-store structure.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/QuantEvolve Automating Quantitative Strategy Discovery through Multi-Agent Evolutionary Framework.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The current survey cites QuantEvolve for from-scratch generation, static role-based model assignment, QD search, and structural references. The paper also directly supports islands, a QD archive, hybrid archive updates, evaluation feedback, and fixed explicit exploration-exploitation control. Verify the static model-role claim: the paper names a two-model ensemble but does not expose per-agent assignment. Generation-mode selection is also underspecified.
